finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF in /preview: a user-supplied URL is fetched with requests.get and the status and first 500 bytes of the response are returned to the caller, so internal responses (including cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254) are readable. Severity HIGH, validation tier 0.

trace.note: target = request.args.get("url", "") takes the value directly from the query string
requests.get(target, timeout=5) issues the request with no scheme, host, or IP validation
jsonify returns resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] to the caller, so the response is readable (non-blind)

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist before the call (no host or scheme check on /preview). No auth on the route. Redirects are followed by default and the redirect target is not re-validated (allow_redirects not set to False). No IP-level block for RFC-1918, loopback, link-local, or metadata addresses. Reachability: no bind address in the repo, so the Flask routes are treated as public ingress (framework default). Triage Step 0 answered (attacker: unauthenticated external user; action: GET /preview?url=...; capability: read internal HTTP responses). No downgrade applied.

verdict.guard_found: none on /preview. The only host check, ALLOWED_HOSTS at app.py:9 and the urlparse/membership test at app.py:23-24, is in the /partner route, not /preview. Redirects are followed by default at app.py:16 with no re-validation, and there is no IP or scheme check.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter at app.py:15 flows unchanged into requests.get at app.py:16 with no validation, and app.py:17 returns the status and body to the caller, so an unauthenticated remote attacker can read internal responses. The claim's "first 500 bytes" is really 500 characters (resp.text[:500]), which is a minor wording error and does not change the verdict.
